seoTitle: Saint Anthony Story for Kids | Catholic Storybook
seoDescription: Ten illustrated pages follow Saint Anthony from Lisbon to Padua: Scripture, changed plans, teaching and practical care. Read or listen together.
intro: Fernando of Lisbon became Anthony, a friar who learned from Scripture and helped others through teaching, prayer and care.
shortAnswer: This ten-page Saint Anthony storybook for ages 6 to 12 follows Anthony from Lisbon and Coimbra through a journey interrupted by illness, years of preaching and teaching, and his life near Padua. The final page invites families to read James 1:22 and turn learning into a small act of care.
summaryHtml: This ten-page story follows Anthony from Lisbon and Coimbra through a journey interrupted by illness, years of preaching and teaching, and his life near Padua. The final page invites families to read James 1:22 and put learning into a small act of care.
familyReadingHtml: With a trusted adult, read James 1:22. This verse asks us to put what we hear into action. Try helping someone at home with a safe, simple task.
aboutHtml:
Illustrations are original imaginative composites, not historical footage or records of private conversations. Modern family scenes invite reflection rather than depict an event from Anthony's life.

Ill children need rest, a trusted adult and medical care. Prayer does not replace practical help or guarantee a missing object, pet or person will be found. Missing-person danger requires adult and trained help immediately. Children are not asked to imitate hazardous travel or martyrdom.

Sources

Benedict XVI: Saint Anthony of Padua

Benedict XVI: Saint Francis of Assisi

James 1:22

faq.q: Who was Saint Anthony of Padua?
faq.a: Born Fernando in Lisbon around 1195, Anthony became a Franciscan friar, preacher and teacher. He died near Padua in 1231.
Children ages 6 to 12, reading or listening with a trusted adult. The final page has a question, Bible reading, safe action and prayer.

faq.q: Does prayer guarantee finding a lost thing?
faq.a: No. Asking Anthony to pray is a devotional practice, not a promise. Practical help matters; a missing person needs immediate adult and trained help.

saintBio.heading: About Saint Anthony of Padua
saintBio.facts:
Lived
c. 1195-1231
Place
Lisbon, Portugal, and Padua, Italy
Status
Canonized 1232 by Pope Gregory IX; Doctor of the Church
Feast
June 13
saintBio.body:
Fernando Martins was born in Lisbon around 1195 and became an Augustinian canon. When the bodies of five Franciscan martyrs from Morocco passed through Coimbra in 1220, he joined the Franciscans and took the name Anthony. He sailed for Morocco, fell ill and ended up in Italy.

For a time he worked in obscurity, until an unplanned sermon at an ordination showed how gifted a preacher he was. Saint Francis made him the first theology teacher of the Franciscans. He preached across France and northern Italy and died near Padua on June 13, 1231, at about 35. He was canonized in 1232 and named a Doctor of the Church in 1946. People ask for his help with lost things, which is a devotion and not a Church title.

Key teaching

Anthony taught the faith by preaching and by teaching theology. His work was to make the Gospel clear to ordinary people.
